articles.title: South Korea’s Kospi index jumps more than 16% on a surge of chipmaking stocks
articles.description: South Korea’s Kospi index has jumped more than 16% as artificial intelligence-related stocks bounced back after losses this week. Shares of South Korean technology giant Samsung Electronics surged over 22%, while memory chipmaker SK Hynix soared nearly 28%. The Kospi index had plummeted more than 16% on Tuesday and Wednesday on a sell-off of technology stocks in part over worries about an AI bubble and rising competition from chipmaking rivals in China. Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 also climbed more than 5% in early Friday trading. Oil prices have fallen, with Brent crude, the international standard, trading at around $86 a barrel. On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 was up 1.7%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.2%. The technology-heavy Nasdaq composite rose 2.8%.

articles.description: Indian benchmark indices opened flat and traded in a choppy, volatile range. Analysts suggest the index may head towards resistance at 24,500-24,600 levels. articles.title: Saudi Arabia announces maritime defence alliance to secure vital waterways
articles.description: Saudi Arabia and 13 other nations have formed a defensive maritime coalition to protect shipping across the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and Gulf of Aden.
